baseline: Initial AI baseline passed 117/117 tests before remediation.
Initial targeted backend queue/proxy baseline passed before remediation.
All core Compose services were healthy before runtime probes.
A real isolated Redis/BullMQ reproduction confirmed that a retained deterministic RAG job ID discarded a later request payload.
Live bidirectional shared-secret probes rejected missing and wrong tokens before resource lookup.

Independent review reproduced eight additional release blockers across lease retry timing, output fencing, redirect-secret handling, compensation ambiguity, embedding integrity, ambiguous commits, route typing, and model transitions; all were fixed and re-reviewed.

scenarios.scenario: Inventory and execute all seven processor classes and their 13 accepted job names
scenarios.expectedResult: Known jobs retry transient failures; unknown names fail once as unrecoverable.
scenarios.failureSignal: Silent acknowledgement or repeated retries of an unsupported job.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Processor unit tests plus full backend suite.

scenarios.scenario: Queue a replacement request while the same resource is actively indexing
scenarios.expectedResult: One active job and one trailing latest job both execute.
scenarios.failureSignal: The later payload is suppressed by a retained job ID.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Isolated live Redis/BullMQ run produced execution order [1, 2].

scenarios.scenario: Two workers attempt to claim one pending lesson, quiz, intervention, or extraction job
scenarios.expectedResult: Exactly one conditional UPDATE succeeds; the loser receives 409.
scenarios.failureSignal: Both workers invoke the model or extraction pipeline.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Concurrent route tests assert one runner invocation and one conflict.

scenarios.scenario: A request is cancelled, a stale worker is reclaimed, or BullMQ redelivers after generated output committed but post-processing failed
scenarios.loadStyle: lease takeover, cancellation, and partial-commit failure injection
scenarios.expectedResult: Only the current persisted worker lease may write; a newer attempt of the same BullMQ job can supersede a timed-out request; committed output is resumed without a second model call.
scenarios.failureSignal: Retries exhaust on 409, a stale worker completes a cancelled job, a poll mutates state, or the model is invoked twice for one durable output.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Lease supersession/fencing, read-only polling, durable cancellation, output-lock ordering, and ambiguous-commit regression tests.

scenarios.scenario: Malformed attempts, stale retries, teacher cancellation, task cancellation, and already-applied records
scenarios.expectedResult: 400 for malformed metadata, atomic retry claims, terminal idempotency, and no false completion.
scenarios.failureSignal: 500 conversion errors, duplicate work, stranded processing, or completed response after cancellation.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Extraction queueing and pipeline regression tests.

scenarios.scenario: One or all query variants fail, the provider changes model, or a malformed vector is returned
scenarios.expectedResult: One strict finite embedding batch, current-model-only vector search, serial DB use, partial results preserved, and a 20-second aggregate deadline.
scenarios.failureSignal: Cross-model comparison, padded vectors, concurrent-session errors, multiplied provider timeouts, or silent empty context.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Dimension/finite checks, model-filter SQL, current-model freshness, one-batch embedding, aggregate timeout, partial, and total-failure tests.

scenarios.scenario: Embedding provider times out during a replacement index
scenarios.expectedResult: No placeholder vector is stored or queried; the prior usable index survives and BullMQ retries.
scenarios.failureSignal: Hash vectors replace semantic vectors, incompatible models are compared, or a failed replacement empties the index.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Provider/degraded-batch rollback, no-DELETE, current-model filtering, and preservation tests.

scenarios.scenario: Ollama times out after grounded citations have been retrieved
scenarios.expectedResult: A visibly degraded, cited, lesson-grounded response is returned.
scenarios.failureSignal: Unhandled timeout or unsupported generated claims.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Tutor and JA timeout regression tests.

scenarios.scenario: Concurrent messages or answer submissions target one session
scenarios.expectedResult: A non-blocking PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock serializes turns before state load or returns 409.
scenarios.failureSignal: Lost round increment, stale latest-state overwrite, or a request blocked beyond its deadline waiting for the lock.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Try-lock-before-load unit test and live PostgreSQL advisory-lock SQL probe.

scenarios.scenario: Missing, wrong, matching, and unconfigured shared-secret cases in both directions
scenarios.expectedResult: Missing/wrong/unconfigured fail before resource access; matching token reaches lookup; signed-storage redirects omit the secret.
scenarios.failureSignal: Forwarded identity is accepted without the secret or a redirect receives the internal token.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Boundary tests, cross-origin redirect capture, and live status probes: AI 401/401/404, backend upload 403/403/404.

scenarios.scenario: AI creates a durable teacher job but Redis enqueue fails
scenarios.expectedResult: Backend atomically marks a still-pending job queueCompensated and returns 503; an ambiguously accepted queue item cannot execute it later.
scenarios.failureSignal: A compensated job is reclaimed after the caller was told queueing failed.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Teacher/extraction compensation marker and terminal-run tests plus controller coverage.

scenarios.scenario: Ollama, embeddings, or response-body streaming approaches route and worker deadlines
scenarios.expectedResult: Chat, tutor start, public generation, and internal workers have explicit tiered deadlines covering headers and body reads; indexing fetches abort.
scenarios.failureSignal: Backend aborts too early, a delayed body escapes the timer, or a worker hangs indefinitely.
scenarios.observabilityEvidence: Proxy and processor delayed-body timeout tests plus abort-signal tests.

findings.title: Retained deterministic indexing IDs suppressed later requests
findings.evidence: Reproduced against real BullMQ; active-only dedup with keepLastIfActive passed a live two-run verification.

findings.title: Teacher and notification custom job IDs used BullMQ-forbidden colons
findings.evidence: IDs now use hyphens and are asserted by producer tests.

findings.title: Teacher AI and extraction jobs could be claimed by concurrent workers
findings.evidence: Conditional UPDATE RETURNING claims persist a unique workerLeaseId, permit one runner, and return 409 to the loser.

findings.title: Process-local startup recovery and polling competed with BullMQ ownership
findings.evidence: Removed process-local task recovery and poll-time status mutation; startup only preloads models, polling is read-only, and BullMQ remains the sole retry owner.

findings.title: Worker lease expiry was shorter than the request budget and writes were not fenced
findings.evidence: Persisted 16-minute leases fence every write; a newer attempt of the same BullMQ job can atomically supersede the prior lease immediately after the 15-minute HTTP timeout instead of exhausting on 409.

findings.title: BullMQ redelivery after output commit could invoke the model twice
findings.evidence: Output commits are lease-guarded and separated from final post-processing; BullMQ redelivery detects and resumes committed output without another generation call.

findings.title: Progress persistence released the final output fence before INSERT
findings.evidence: Progress now commits before the final FOR UPDATE; the lease/cancellation lock remains held continuously through output INSERT and commit.

findings.title: Inner generation retries could duplicate output after an ambiguous commit
findings.evidence: A durable HTTP execution attempts output generation once; BullMQ owns retry and each redelivery checks for committed output before invoking the generator.

findings.title: Internal teacher runners did not validate durable job type
findings.evidence: Lesson, quiz, and intervention routes reject a valid UUID whose persisted job_type does not match the route before any claim or model call.

findings.title: Teacher AI helper failures were swallowed before BullMQ retry
findings.evidence: All generation helpers persist failure metadata and rethrow; focused tests cover lesson, quiz, and intervention.

findings.title: Successful durable job creation could be orphaned by Redis enqueue failure
findings.evidence: Pending-only compensation avoids overwriting a claimed job, lesson/quiz/intervention handoffs all compensate enqueue failure, and backend returns 503.

findings.title: Ambiguously accepted queue jobs could execute after compensation returned 503
findings.evidence: Compensation atomically persists queueCompensated on a still-pending teacher/extraction job, and internal runners treat the marker as terminal.

findings.title: Shared-secret checks were optional on proxied user-context routes
findings.evidence: Both services now fail closed; AI uses constant-time comparison; live bidirectional probes pass.

findings.title: Backend upload redirects forwarded the internal shared secret to storage
findings.evidence: The authenticated first hop disables redirects; validated HTTP(S) storage redirects are fetched without X-Internal-Service-Token, including subsequent redirects.

findings.title: Indexing workers had no HTTP deadline
findings.evidence: AbortController deadlines remain active through response-body parsing, normalize timeout errors, and rethrow for exponential retry.

findings.title: Class and library indexing transaction boundaries could lose usable vectors
findings.evidence: Class reindex takes a per-class transaction advisory lock and commits; library replacement embeds before atomic delete/insert and rolls back on failure.

findings.title: Retrieval and index-status code shared AsyncSession across concurrent tasks
findings.evidence: Variants embed in one batch, DB operations are serial under a 20-second aggregate deadline, and partial degradation remains observable.

findings.title: Placeholder and cross-model vectors could silently corrupt semantic retrieval
findings.evidence: Hash fallback was removed; vector count, exact dimension, and finite values are enforced; failed indexing preserves the old index; retrieval and class freshness use only the current embedding_model.

findings.title: Tutor and JA grounded calls propagated Ollama timeouts
findings.evidence: Both return explicit degraded responses that preserve citations and avoid new unsupported claims.

findings.title: Concurrent tutor turns could overwrite latest session state
findings.evidence: Per-user/session PostgreSQL transaction try-lock is acquired before loading mutable state; overlap fails promptly with 409.

findings.title: Performance recompute coalesced different student subsets
findings.evidence: Stable hash of the sorted unique student set is now part of the time-window job ID.

findings.title: Unknown BullMQ job names were acknowledged as successful
findings.evidence: All seven processor classes now reject unsupported contracts with UnrecoverableError.

findings.title: Queue handoff after non-AI domain commits lacks a transactional outbox
findings.evidence: A crash or Redis outage between domain persistence and queue insertion can still require reconciliation; a shared outbox is a schema-level redesign.

findings.title: Runtime payload schemas are duplicated across backend and AI service
findings.evidence: Current tests cover exercised envelopes, but generated cross-service contract fixtures are not yet present.

findings.title: Production-scale Ollama saturation and long-document memory pressure remain unmeasured
findings.evidence: Failure paths are deterministic and verified locally; a staging soak with production models and representative PDFs is still required.

changesMade: Hardened all seven BullMQ processor classes, job IDs, retry propagation, active-only deduplication, and unsupported-contract handling.
Made BullMQ the sole durable execution owner; removed process-local recovery and poll-time state mutation.
Added persisted worker leases, same-BullMQ newer-attempt supersession, and fenced claims, progress, output, completion, failure, and cancellation writes.
Made committed generation output resumable on redelivery, kept the final output lock through commit, and removed inner retries around ambiguous output commits.
Added strict worker metadata/job-type validation, durable cancellation, terminal queue-compensation markers, and quiz retry compensation.
Added tiered backend-to-AI deadlines that include response-body reads plus abortable indexing calls with exponential BullMQ retries.
Made the shared-secret boundary fail closed and stripped the internal token before following signed-storage redirects.

Made class/library index replacement transaction-safe and removed unsafe placeholder embeddings; retrieval enforces exact finite dimensions, current-model vector filtering, one batch, serial DB work, and an aggregate deadline.
Added grounded tutor and JA fallbacks plus non-blocking per-session concurrency serialization.

Cancellation and output commits survive process restart and BullMQ redelivery.
Slow requests terminate through body parsing and retry instead of hanging.
Model timeouts return grounded fallbacks where safe; embedding outages preserve the prior index and return no incompatible context.
The service boundary no longer accepts forwarded identity without the shared secret or leaks it to storage redirects.
Replacement indexing preserves the previous usable vector set on failure and serializes same-class replacement.
unchanged: Backend remains the public auth/RBAC and durable orchestration owner.
AI service remains assistive and does not mutate official grades or enrollment.
Existing public response envelopes remain compatible; degraded fields are additive.
remainingRisks: Non-AI queue handoffs still need a transactional outbox or periodic reconciliation for crash consistency.

Cross-service runtime schemas remain manually synchronized.
An embedding-model change safely hides old library vectors, but operators must run library backfill to restore that context.

Keep active-only BullMQ deduplication with one trailing replacement for indexing.
Keep fail-closed shared-secret checks and tiered deadlines.
Keep deterministic degraded generation responses only where grounded evidence remains available; never synthesize semantic vectors.
Keep strict finite current-model embeddings, one-batch retrieval, aggregate deadlines, and non-blocking advisory locks.

Add periodic reconciliation for failed or missed RAG/library enqueue operations.
Trigger or require a library backfill whenever the configured embedding model changes.
